description: BIShare costs nothing. Unlimited device-to-device transfers, encrypted links up to 100 GB, no account, no subscription, no ads. Open source under MIT.
heading: Free. All of it.

included.network: Unlimited transfers between nearby devices — no size cap at all
included.e2e: End-to-end encrypted on every path, including links
included.links: Encrypted share links up to 100 GB, with QR and 6-character codes
included.expire: Links auto-expire after 24 hours; nothing is kept
included.rooms: Rooms — share with a group over one short code
included.platforms: iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux
included.source: Open source under the MIT licence — no ads, no tracking

ctaNote: There is no paid tier, and none planned. Nothing here is a trial.

compare.title: What the alternatives charge
compare.note: Competitor prices are their published list prices and change over time; check their sites for current figures.

why.a: Because it costs us almost nothing to run. Nearby transfers go straight between your devices and never touch a server, so the expensive part of file sharing simply does not happen. Links stream through storage in chunks and delete themselves after 24 hours, which keeps that side to pennies. The size caps other services impose are pricing decisions, not physics — and BIShare is open source, so you can read the code that proves it.

catch.a: There is no catch, and that is checkable rather than a promise: the source is public under MIT, there are no ads, no tracking, and no account to create — so there is no profile to sell. Files sent over your own network never reach us at all, and files sent by link are encrypted before they leave your device, so we hold bytes we cannot read.

limits.a: Transfers between devices on the same network have no size limit — the ceiling is the receiving device's free space. Share links carry up to 100 GB per transfer and expire after 24 hours. Both are free, with no account on either end.

later.a: There is no paid tier today and none planned. If a paid service is ever added it would be something new alongside this, not a wall placed around what already works — and because the project is MIT-licensed, the version you have today stays free regardless.
